name: Sam Gallucci
current_role: Pastor and nonprofit founder in Oxnard
bio: Sam Gallucci is a longtime Oxnard resident who began his career at IBM and later became an executive vice president at PeopleSoft before moving into ministry. He was most recently senior pastor of Embrace! Church and founded nonprofits including The Kingdom Center, Treasured Harvest and Revive Academies. He describes his fiscal views as conservative and says he wants to reduce political division.

platform.point: Backs a 'National Settlement on Immigration': remove criminal offenders, expand work permits where labor is short.
Tie federal homelessness funds to results and let cities clear encampments while offering services.
Defend SNAP while cutting wasteful spending; give small businesses tax relief and deregulation.
Make parents' rights the guiding principle and end federal funding for DEI and CRT programs.
Add resources for local policing and fentanyl interdiction, and ban cashless bail.
Ban stock trading by members of Congress.
Expand child tax credits and lower prescription prices through most-favored-nation pricing.
Voiced full support for the Trump administration's military operations in Iran at a May 2026 debate.

economy.evidence: Campaign site calls for small-business tax relief and deregulation, while also backing incentives for domestic manufacturing.

welfare.evidence: Pledges to defend SNAP and expand child tax credits, but wants homelessness funding tied to measurable results.

liberty.evidence: LGBTQ: would use federal funding to keep transgender women out of women's sports; also stresses parental rights; no stated abortion, gun or drug positions.

security.evidence: Calls for more resources for local policing and gang task forces and a ban on cashless bail.

immigration.evidence: Supports funding mass removal of criminal immigrants while streamlining work permits and case-managed off-ramps for people with deep community ties.

foreign.evidence: At a May 2026 debate he gave unqualified support to U.S. military operations in Iran.

energy.evidence: At a May 2026 debate he called California's cuts to rooftop solar incentives a failure for climate efforts.

education.evidence: Names parents' rights as his guiding principle in education and wants to end federal funding for DEI and CRT programs; founded a low-cost alternative school network.

faith.evidence: General statement: a pastor whose campaign slogan is 'Faith. Family. Freedom. Future.' and who proposes partnering with faith communities on anti-trafficking work.

notes: Read the campaign site's home and newsroom pages, a May 2026 Ventura County Star debate report and Acorn coverage. No positions on tech regulation were found.

name: Eric Ching
bio: Eric Ching has served on the Walnut City Council since 2012, including a term as mayor in 2016–2017, after leading the Chinese American Association of Walnut. He is a business owner with a background in telecommunications and IT management. He ran for Congress in California's 38th district in 2022 and 2024.

platform.point: Pledges to defend First Amendment freedoms and the right to keep and bear arms.
Secure the border against smuggling of weapons, drugs and people while promoting legal trade and tourism.
Supports term limits for federal, state and local officials and reasonable pay for officials.
Tough-on-crime deterrence, restitution from offenders and financial help for crime victims.
Encourage treatment centers for people facing substance abuse and homelessness tied to mental illness.
Supports school choice and opposes identity-based admissions and racially divisive curriculum.
Remove burdensome regulations and protect U.S. businesses and workers from unfair practices.

economy.evidence: General statement: pledges to remove burdensome regulations on businesses.

liberty.evidence: General statement on guns and speech: pledges to support the right to keep and bear arms and First Amendment freedoms; no abortion or LGBTQ stance found.

security.evidence: General statement: backs tough-on-crime deterrence while also pledging to protect rights against unreasonable searches.

immigration.evidence: General statement: wants to secure the border against illegal movement of people and contraband while promoting legal trade and tourism.

education.evidence: General statement: campaign site says he supports school choice and parental rights and opposes identity-based admissions policies.

notes: Read the campaign site's full content (about, priorities, endorsements) and searched news and voter guides; no questionnaire answers were found. Positions on health care, foreign policy, energy, tech and religion in public life remain unknown.

name: Sydney Kamlager-Dove
bio: Sydney Kamlager-Dove has represented California's 37th district since 2023 and sits on the Foreign Affairs and Judiciary committees. Born in Chicago, she studied at USC and Carnegie Mellon, worked in child care advocacy, and served as a Los Angeles Community College District trustee and in the California Assembly and Senate.

platform.point: Co-authored California's CROWN Act banning discrimination based on natural hairstyles.
Has backed police use-of-force standards and restoring voting rights for people on parole.
Serves as ranking member of the Foreign Affairs subcommittee on South and Central Asia.
Introduced the LINE Act to bar sharing Medicaid data with immigration enforcement agencies.
Introduced the CLEAN Energy NOW Acts with Reps. Ocasio-Cortez and Ross to ease solar and wind permitting.
Co-authored California's AB 1400 guaranteed health care for all bill as a state legislator.
Says her long-term goal is free universal preschool and free education through college.
Supports abortion access and fought to stop California insurers from charging for abortion services.

economy.evidence: Campaign lists her work extending California's earned income tax credit and votes for the Tenant Protection Act and an eviction moratorium.

welfare.evidence: Co-authored California's AB 1400 guaranteed health care for all bill and backs free child care and preschool slots.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: former Planned Parenthood Los Angeles board member who supports abortion access and fought insurer charges for abortion.

security.evidence: Advocated stronger statewide standards for police use of force.

immigration.evidence: Introduced the LINE Act to stop Medicaid data from being shared with immigration agencies and criticized ICE raids.

foreign.evidence: Describes Israel as a democracy to support, while voting against a resolution on the 'river to the sea' phrase.

energy.evidence: Joined a coalition seeking 100% renewable energy by 2030 and introduced the CLEAN Energy NOW Acts.

education.evidence: Campaign states a goal of free universal preschool and free education through college, and backed free community college.

notes: Reviewed the campaign priorities and about pages, House press releases, a sponsored-bill list and Wikipedia; congress.gov and GovTrack blocked access. No public positions on tech regulation or religion in public life were found.

name: Samantha Mota
bio: Samantha Mota is a Los Angeles County native and community activist running for California's 37th district. She served on Santa Monica's Public Safety Reform and Oversight Commission and has worked on urban agriculture efforts.

platform.point: Makes universal health care a top campaign priority.
Runs on a 'Housing for All' agenda to expand access to affordable homes.
Calls for dismantling ICE and ending for-profit immigration detention.
Supports the Raise the Wage Act, higher corporate tax rates and a larger Earned Income Tax Credit.
Would end foreign aid with a total arms embargo and repeal FISA and the AUMF.
Promotes the Green New Deal and more green space in underserved neighborhoods.
Opposes all school vouchers and backs full IDEA funding and universal school meals.
Seeks national paid family leave of up to a year and a $5,000 child tax credit expansion.

economy.evidence: Issue page backs the Raise the Wage Act, higher corporate tax rates and an expanded EITC, alongside small-business tax cuts.

welfare.evidence: Campaign makes universal health care a top priority.

security.evidence: Pledges to repeal FISA and co-sponsor bills ending warrantless surveillance of citizens.

immigration.evidence: Issue page calls for dismantling ICE, ending for-profit detention and expanding access to asylum.

foreign.evidence: Calls for ending foreign aid with a total arms embargo and rescinding the AUMF.

energy.evidence: Pledges to promote the Green New Deal.

education.evidence: Opposes all school vouchers and supports full IDEA funding and stronger Title I.

notes: Read every issue page on the campaign site; none address abortion, guns, LGBTQ rights, tech regulation or religion, so those topics remain unscored.

name: Pedro Antonio Casas
current_role: Retired U.S. Army colonel and psychologist
bio: Pedro Antonio Casas is a clinical, forensic and aero-medical psychologist and retired U.S. Army colonel who served from 1994 to 2023, including three wartime deployments. He holds a Ph.D. from UC Santa Barbara and says he grew up in Baldwin Park. He has not held elected office.

platform.point: Calls fixing immigration his first priority and opposes sanctuary cities.
Proposes tax cuts and less regulation on small businesses to spur growth.
Believes life begins at conception, with exceptions for sexual assault or the mother's life.
Supports eliminating the U.S. Department of Education and returning control to states.
Wants audits of every federal program and cuts in spending to reduce the debt.
Pledges to combat fentanyl trafficking across the southern border.
Opposes new gun restrictions, citing the Second Amendment.
Wants athletes to compete only against others of the same biological sex.

economy.evidence: Strongly disagrees with higher taxes on those who can afford them and strongly agrees with cutting spending.

welfare.evidence: Would keep Medicaid and Medicare but says no other taxpayer-funded health programs are needed.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: says life begins at conception and backs enforcing the Comstock Act; LGBTQ: opposes gender transition for minors and same-sex marriage; guns: opposes any restrictions.

immigration.evidence: Strongly opposes sanctuary cities and calls fixing immigration his first priority.

foreign.evidence: Calls the U.S.-Israel relationship critically important and views China as a serious threat; favors flexible foreign policy.

tech.evidence: Strongly agrees government must protect children from online sexual exploitation.

education.evidence: Strongly supports eliminating the U.S. Department of Education and returning control to states.

faith.evidence: Rejects strict church-state separation, backs religious exemptions from providing services, and cites Catholic beliefs.

notes: Used the campaign site and his own iVoterGuide questionnaire answers; Vote-USA had no statements. His energy answer named only nuclear power, and no surveillance or policing-powers stance was found.

name: Cristian Morales
bio: Cristian Morales was born in Guatemala and holds a management degree from Purdue and a master's in industrial and labor relations from Cornell. He has spent more than 20 years in manufacturing, including automotive, aerospace and defense, and ran for governor in California's 2021 recall election.

platform.point: Cut taxes and unnecessary regulations and bring manufacturing back to America.
Boost housing supply by easing permitting and zoning rules and opening suitable federal land.
Secure the border while supporting legal immigration and protecting DREAMers.
Supports school choice across public, charter, private and vocational options.
Keep the U.S. ahead of China on AI and criminalize AI-generated child sexual abuse material.
Supports an all-of-the-above energy strategy and expanding nuclear power.
Ban members of Congress from trading individual stocks.
Peace through strength: strong alliances, a tough approach to China and support for Israel.

economy.evidence: Platform calls for tax and regulation cuts; strongly disagrees with raising taxes on those who can afford it.

welfare.evidence: Would keep Medicaid and Medicare but sees no need for other taxpayer-funded health programs.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: protect life from conception with exceptions; guns: opposes restrictions; LGBTQ: opposes youth transition and same-sex marriage.

immigration.evidence: Opposes sanctuary cities and wants border enforcement, but supports legal immigration and protecting DREAMers.

foreign.evidence: Chose 'intervene whenever freedom is threatened' in his questionnaire; platform backs strong alliances but warns against endless wars.

energy.evidence: Backs an all-of-the-above strategy including oil and gas and fewer regulations that raise energy prices.

tech.evidence: Platform backs reasonable AI safeguards without hurting innovation; questionnaire says parents, not government, lead on children's online safety.

education.evidence: Supports eliminating the U.S. Department of Education and school choice for parents.

faith.evidence: Says church-state separation should not remove school prayer or religious displays and opposes forcing services against religious beliefs.

notes: Found his campaign site (forallvoices.com) and his own iVoterGuide answers. No clear stance on surveillance or police powers was found.

name: Nanette Barragán
bio: Nanette Barragán has represented California's 44th district since 2017, sits on the Energy and Commerce Committee, and chaired the Congressional Hispanic Caucus from 2023 to 2025. She holds degrees from UCLA and USC law school, and earlier served on the Hermosa Beach City Council and worked as an attorney at Latham & Watkins and in the Clinton White House.

platform.point: Seeks a ban on hydrofluoric acid at oil refineries near populated areas.
Supports abortion rights and opposed the Dobbs decision.
Voted for the Inflation Reduction Act's clean-energy investments.
Supports raising the minimum wage to $15 an hour and keeping Davis-Bacon protections.
Co-leads the HEAL for Immigrant Families Act to remove barriers to health coverage for immigrants.
Supports closing background check loopholes and banning devices that make rifles fire automatically.
Wants federally backed public schools, funded early education and lower college costs.
Member of the Medicare for All Caucus and a defender of the Affordable Care Act.

economy.evidence: Supports raising the minimum wage to $15 an hour and voted for the Inflation Reduction Act.

welfare.evidence: Member of the Medicare for All Caucus; official site calls health care a fundamental right.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: opposed the Dobbs ruling and holds a 100% NARAL rating; guns: backs universal background checks and a bump-stock ban.

security.evidence: Spoke on the House floor for the George Floyd Justice in Policing Act.

immigration.evidence: Campaign backs a path to citizenship and the DREAM Act; co-leads the HEAL for Immigrant Families Act.

energy.evidence: Pushes refinery hydrofluoric-acid ban and environmental rules; voted for the Inflation Reduction Act.

education.evidence: Official site stresses federal support for free public education, early education funding and affordable college.

notes: Reviewed official issue pages, the campaign issues page, Wikipedia and a 2025 press release; congress.gov was blocked. Her foreign policy page covers only cybersecurity and ports, and no tech-regulation or religion positions were found.

name: Genevieve Angel
current_role: Family nurse practitioner and small-business owner
bio: Genevieve Angel is a family nurse practitioner, healthcare executive and small-business owner who moved from Manila and has lived in Lakewood for nearly 30 years. She holds a nursing degree from the University of Santo Tomas, an MBA and an MSN, and is a first-time candidate.

platform.point: Lower the cost of living and expand economic opportunity for working families.
Opposes higher taxes on high earners and favors tax cuts and deregulation, including permitting reform.
Lower out-of-pocket costs and expand access while federal aid focuses on seniors, disabled and low-income people.
Shift toward merit-based immigration and end sanctuary cities.
Personally pro-life but opposes a federal abortion mandate, leaving the issue to states.
Peace through strength, including helping those resisting tyranny and a strong alliance with Israel.
Sees coal and nuclear as the most reliable power sources for growing demand.
Return education decisions to states, local school boards and parents.

economy.evidence: Strongly opposes higher taxes on those who can afford them and backs tax cuts and deregulation.

welfare.evidence: Says federal aid should focus on seniors, disabled and low-income people while cutting other social spending.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: pro-life with exceptions but leaves it to states; guns: opposes disarming law-abiding citizens; LGBTQ: opposes youth transition and same-sex marriage.

immigration.evidence: Favors merit-based over family-based immigration and strongly opposes sanctuary cities.

foreign.evidence: Backs helping countries fight tyranny and calls the U.S.-Israel alliance a strategic and moral imperative.

energy.evidence: Names coal and nuclear as the most reliable sources and wants fewer rules on fossil-fuel refineries.

tech.evidence: Says parents, not government, should lead on protecting children online.

education.evidence: Agrees with eliminating the U.S. Department of Education and handing control to states and parents.

faith.evidence: Supports allowing acknowledgment of a supreme being in classrooms but says people should not impose beliefs on others.

notes: Used the campaign site's home, priorities and about pages plus her own iVoterGuide answers; LocalCandidates.org was behind a bot check and was skipped. No stance on surveillance or police powers was found.
